sources.entry: Maza ad blocking - Local ad blocker. Like Pi-hole but local and using your operating system. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Shell

summary.one_liner: A bash script that blocks ads system-wide by managing the operating system's hosts file (and optionally dnsmasq), so every browser and app benefits without extensions.
summary.what_it_does: Maza is a command-line tool (the `maza` command) that downloads a list of ad and tracking domains and writes them into the system hosts file so they resolve to nothing. Commands cover updating the domain database, starting, stopping, and checking status. Users can add their own domains to block, or list domains to ignore, and can switch to a different source list such as Steven Black's. For wildcard (subdomain) blocking, the README describes an optional setup using dnsmasq, with instructions for macOS and Debian/Ubuntu Linux, including pointing the OS DNS settings at the local server. A daily cron job can keep the list updated. The README also describes a tutorial for building a Pi-hole-style DNS server on a Raspberry Pi or VPS.
use_cases: block ads in every browser without extensions
block ads system-wide on macOS or Linux
block ads on a Windows Subsystem for Linux setup
keep the ad-blocking domain list updated automatically
run a local Pi-hole alternative with dnsmasq
block custom domains or whitelist domains from blocking
how_to_run: Install gnu-sed on macOS: brew install gnu-sed
Download and install the script: curl -o maza && sudo rm -rf /usr/local/bin/maza && chmod +x maza && sudo mv maza /usr/local/bin
Back up your hosts file: sudo cp /etc/hosts /etc/hosts.backup
Update the domain database: sudo maza update
notable: Works system-wide through the OS hosts file, so it affects any browser or application without installing extensions
Single bash script with commands for update, start, stop, and status
Optional dnsmasq mode adds wildcard/subdomain blocking, which the hosts file cannot do
Supports custom block lists and an ignore list for domains that should not be blocked
Includes a tutorial for running it as a self-hosted Pi-hole-style DNS server
caveats: The hosts file does not support wildcard subdomains; full DNS-level filtering requires installing and configuring dnsmasq manually
macOS needs gnu-sed installed and extra cron PATH settings for automatic updates
Default list is small (about 3.7k domains); larger lists must be set up manually
